Problem Statement:
✨ Allow using dependables with `functools.partial()`

Discussion: https://github.com/tiangolo/fastapi/discussions/9744

Using `functools.partial()` with dependables feels like a very obvious idiom. `partial()` already works for dependables that are plain function, but it doesn't work consistently, partial of async and callable classes didn't work consistently.

This PR makes partial() work consistently in all combinations.

turns.reply:
Dependables wrapped in `functools.partial()` now behave the same as plain functions, async functions, and callable classes; the patch is submitted.

The cause was that `inspect.unwrap()` does not look through partials, so FastAPI classified a partial by its own `__call__` and missed async and generator callables underneath. The fix unwraps partials in `_unwrapped_call` (`fastapi/dependencies/models.py`) and in `get_typed_signature` (`fastapi/dependencies/utils.py`).

I checked a partial of an async function, a partial of an async callable instance, and a partial of a sync callable instance inside one endpoint, and the values came out right. `tests/test_dependency_class.py` (8 tests) and `tests/test_dependency_contextmanager.py` (22 tests) pass. I did not add new tests, and the repo's `tests/test_dependency_types.py` rename from the issue is not present, so I did not run that file.
